prompt: Before any admin configuration, the front page listed only Groups and Users. Why not Events?
hint: What has to happen for a model to appear?

choices.text: The superuser lacked permission to see events
choices.why: A superuser has every permission.

choices.text: Nothing had registered it
choices.why: Right. The admin shows only what it was told about.

choices.text: The events app was missing from INSTALLED_APPS
choices.why: It was there since lesson 2.

choices.text: Events had no migrations applied yet, so their table did not exist
choices.why: Lesson 4 applied them.

prompt: Logging in with curl took a GET of the login page before the POST. What did the GET provide?

choices.text: The session cookie that proves who you are
choices.why: That arrives after the POST succeeds.

choices.text: A one-time password
choices.why: The admin has no second factor of its own.

choices.text: The csrftoken cookie
choices.why: Right, to send back with its token; the POST is refused without it.

choices.text: The next parameter
choices.why: next was typed into the POST by hand.

prompt: Why does the lesson suggest typing createsuperuser interactively on your own machine rather than with the password in the command?
hint: Where does a command line end up?

choices.text: So the password stays out of the screen and the shell's history
choices.why: Right. The course used the other form only to be reproducible.

choices.text: Because --noinput creates an account without a password
choices.why: It read DJANGO_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD.

choices.text: Because the interactive form hashes the password and the other does not
choices.why: Both hash it.

choices.text: Because only the interactive form sets is_staff
choices.why: Both create a superuser, which is staff.

prompt: After admin.site.register(Event), each row of the list showed the event's title. Where did that come from?

choices.text: The first CharField of the model
choices.why: The admin does not pick a field by position.

choices.text: The slug, turned into words
choices.why: The slug is not used for display.

choices.text: The model's __str__ method
choices.why: Right: Event.__str__. Without it the row would read Event object (1).

choices.text: The template of lesson 3
choices.why: The admin uses its own templates.

prompt: Match each admin page to the permission it checks.
hint: The figure of the registering section.

prompt: What does the admin's delete page show before it deletes an event with registrations?

choices.text: Nothing: it deletes at once
choices.why: It always asks.

choices.text: An error, because registrations point at the event
choices.why: CASCADE allows it.

choices.text: Only the event's title
choices.why: It shows more than that.

choices.text: What else goes with it, and asks
choices.why: Right: the registrations deleted with it, because the foreign key says CASCADE.

prompt: The Seats taken column comes from a method. Why does get_queryset annotate the count?

choices.text: Methods in list_display cannot run queries
choices.why: They can, which is the problem.

choices.text: So the whole list costs one query, not one per row
choices.why: Right, and it makes the column sortable.

choices.text: The admin caches annotations between requests
choices.why: Nothing is cached.

choices.text: Count is the only way to read related rows
choices.why: There are several; this is the cheapest here.

prompt: Match each ModelAdmin option to what it adds to the list page.

pairs.right: the sidebar of links to narrow the list
links by year, month and day

prompt: Searching the events list for dojo found 1 result. Out of how many events in total?
An organiser adds event.organiser.email to list_display, and the list gets slower as events grow. What fixes it?
hint: Each row reads a related object.

choices.text: Raising list_per_page
choices.why: More rows per page makes it worse.

choices.text: Adding organiser to search_fields
choices.why: Searching does not change how rows are loaded.

choices.text: list_select_related
choices.why: Right: the join goes into the list's one query, lesson 4's select_related.

choices.text: Caching the admin page in nginx
choices.why: A cache would hide data an organiser needs current.

prompt: What does RegistrationInline add to an event's change page?

choices.text: A table of its registrations
choices.why: Right, editable, with a Delete box per row.

choices.text: A link to the registrations list, filtered
choices.why: That would be a filter; the inline embeds the rows.

choices.text: A count of seats taken
choices.why: That is the list's column.

choices.text: A CSV download
choices.why: That is the action.

prompt: How did the admin know which registrations belong on the Testing dojo's page?

choices.text: From related_name in the inline's options
choices.why: related_name is on the model; the inline needs nothing.

choices.text: By matching the slug in the email address
choices.why: Nothing matches by text.

choices.text: From the foreign key, and nothing else
choices.why: Right. Two foreign keys to Event would need fk_name.

choices.text: From the order the rows were created
choices.why: Order does not join anything.

prompt: What does an admin action receive?

choices.text: A list of ids as strings
choices.why: Django turns them into a QuerySet first.

choices.text: The ticked rows, as a QuerySet
choices.why: Right, with the ModelAdmin and the request; its return value is the response.

choices.text: One row at a time, in a loop Django runs
choices.why: It gets them all at once.

choices.text: Only the request; it must read the ids itself
choices.why: The QuerySet is ready for it.

prompt: An action that emails every registered person is ticked on all events. What does the lesson advise?
hint: How many rows can be ticked?

choices.text: Limit actions to one row with list_per_page
choices.why: list_per_page does not limit selection across pages.

choices.text: Nothing: the request waits until the emails are sent
choices.why: That request could take minutes and time out.

choices.text: Hand the work to a background task
choices.why: Right, lesson 13.

choices.text: Run it only as a superuser
choices.why: Who runs it does not change how long it takes.

prompt: Every model's list page starts with one action: Delete ___.
Which flag must be true for a user to log into the admin at all?

choices.text: is_active alone
choices.why: An active user who is not staff is turned away.

choices.text: is_staff
choices.why: Right. Permissions then decide what they see.

choices.text: is_admin
choices.why: There is no such flag.

choices.text: is_organiser
choices.why: Groups are not flags on the user.

prompt: Bruno is staff, in Organisers, with view_event, change_event and view_registration. Which of these does he get? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: The events list, with a Change link
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The delete page of an event
choices.why: It answered 403.

choices.text: The registrations list, read-only
choices.why: Right: View.

choices.text: The list of users
choices.why: Not in his group; 403.

choices.text: An Add link for events
choices.why: add_event is not his.

prompt: Why give permissions to a group rather than to each organiser?

choices.text: Users cannot hold permissions directly
choices.why: They can; groups are about writing the rule once.

choices.text: So the organisers' rule is written once
choices.why: Right. People join and leave the group.

choices.text: Groups bypass is_staff
choices.why: Nothing bypasses is_staff.

choices.text: Group permissions are checked faster
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

prompt: A colleague pastes Bruno the delete link of an event from their own screen. What happens when he opens it?

choices.text: The page opens, because the link carries the colleague's session
choices.why: Links carry no session.

choices.text: The event is deleted at once
choices.why: A delete page asks first, and Bruno cannot reach it.

choices.text: 403 Forbidden, from the admin
choices.why: Right. Every request is checked against his own permissions.

choices.text: A redirect to the login page
choices.why: He is logged in; he lacks the permission.

prompt: After the admin's add form saved Elisa, how many registrations did the 12-seat workshop have?
Why did the unique constraint still hold in the admin while the capacity rule did not?

choices.text: Only one of them lives in the database
choices.why: Right. Whoever writes the row meets the constraint; the capacity rule is in a function the admin never calls.

choices.text: The admin checks uniqueness but skips counts to stay fast
choices.why: The admin knows nothing of either rule; the database does.

choices.text: Superusers are exempt from capacity
choices.why: Nobody is exempt; the rule was never called.

choices.text: The lock expired
choices.why: No lock was ever taken.

prompt: Which change did agenda make so the admin cannot add registrations?

choices.text: Removed Registration from the admin
choices.why: Organisers still see and cancel registrations there.

choices.text: Took add_registration away from the superuser
choices.why: A superuser has every permission whatever you do.

choices.text: has_add_permission returning False
choices.why: Right, on the inline and on RegistrationAdmin.

choices.text: A CHECK constraint on capacity
choices.why: A CHECK sees one row; capacity depends on many.

prompt: Which of these does the lesson recommend for guarding the admin? Choose all that apply.
hint: Moving the address is not a defence on its own.

choices.text: Serving it only over HTTPS
choices.why: Right, lesson 16.

choices.text: Few staff accounts with narrow groups
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Moving it to a secret address and relying on that
choices.why: That only stops automated guessing.

choices.text: A second factor, from a library such as django-otp
choices.why: Right; the admin has none of its own.

choices.text: Giving visitors staff accounts to edit their own data
choices.why: Visitors never get staff accounts.

prompt: Put the steps of giving a new organiser access in order.
items: log in as them and read the front page

prompt: A team wants organisers to add walk-in attendees in the admin without breaking the capacity rule. Which approach keeps the rule?
hint: Send the admin through the same door.

choices.text: Trust organisers to count before adding
choices.why: A rule that depends on people remembering is not a rule.

choices.text: Call register() from the admin too
choices.why: Right, from save_model or a form's clean: one function, one lock, every door.

choices.text: Raise every event's capacity by a few seats
choices.why: That moves the limit; it does not enforce it.

choices.text: Give organisers superuser accounts
choices.why: That widens access and still skips the rule.
